_comment: Agent registry. Use a short alias with --agents instead of a full spec.
Aliases resolve to '<provider>:<model-id>'. Groups expand to several.
Only tool-calling CHAT models belong here: classifiers (prompt-guard,
gpt-oss-safeguard) and speech/image/embedding models cannot act as agents.
GROQ IS THE DEFAULT PROVIDER for this study: its free tier is the only
one of the four that sustains a full grid. OpenAI has no credit on this
key and Gemini's free tier caps at 20 requests/day, which is under one
condition of one model.
Groq free-tier limits that shape the design. The binding one is TOKENS
PER MINUTE, not per day: gpt-oss-120b is 8,000 TPM, so ~1k-token calls
allow about 7 requests/minute. --rpm alone cannot respect this (25 rpm
x 1k tokens = 25k TPM, 3x over); the 'tpm' limits below are enforced by
holding requests back until the sliding 60s window has room.
openai/gpt-oss-120b  8,000 TPM, ~200k tokens/day -> ~1 grid/day
openai/gpt-oss-20b   8,000 TPM, cheaper per episode
qwen/qwen3.8-27b     1,000 output-TPM, below one episode's budget.
NOT in any group; every call 429s.
VERIFY YOUR OWN LIMITS at console.groq.com -- they are account-specific.
A wrong tpm here only costs throughput: the in-request 429 handler waits
out whatever the provider actually enforces.
The cross-family aliases below are UNVERIFIED against the live catalog.
Run `python list_models.py groq` and keep only the ids it prints. A
cross-FAMILY comparison (gpt-oss vs llama) is worth more to a reviewer
than two sizes of one family, because a size difference confounds
capability with post-training policy.
Pin dated ids where the provider offers them. A floating alias such as
gemini-flash-latest or gpt-4.1-mini silently changes model under you and
makes Appendix A unreproducible; record the serving backend there too.
Gemini ids are listed as 'models/<id>' but called as '<id>'.
limits: per-model max_tokens, needed because Groq refuses an uncapped
request from a reasoning model on the free tier.
hf_* aliases use Hugging Face Inference Providers, a ROUTER. Free HF
accounts get NO Inference Providers credits (PRO gets $2/month), so
these are NOT a free-tier substitute for Groq. Use them only to reach a
model FAMILY that Groq does not host. A ":groq" suffix just routes back
to Groq and spends HF credit for nothing. Ids are UNVERIFIED: run
`python list_models.py hf` and keep only what your token can reach.
SWITCHING MODELS is the only thing that should change between runs.
The suite, the policy and the metric definitions are pinned by the
dataset/metric digests in pda/freeze.py, so `--agents X` vs `--agents Y`
is a model comparison and nothing else. To add a model: put an alias
here. To add a PROVIDER: one line in PROVIDERS in run_audit.py, giving
its OpenAI-compatible base_url and the env var holding its key (empty
string = keyless local server).
ollama:* aliases are LOCAL: no key, no quota, no rate limit. Use them to
develop and to run unlimited grids. qwen7 points at the num_ctx 8192
build created with `ollama create qwen2.5-detour -f configs/models/Modelfile`; the raw
qwen7raw has Ollama's default context, which silently truncates the
denial out of a long transcript.
